attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter post.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps 'based on my research', the one-year scope and the 'think' qualifier on intent. It reports what he could not account for rather than stating a firm ceiling.

contract.note: Reading his words as implying no more than 500MW of operational capacity is the ordinary reading, given the surrounding text. The contract rightly separates the intent allegation and says ambiguous disclosure cannot prove it.

evidence.note: Microsoft says it added nearly 1GW of 'total capacity' in one quarter. This is a company disclosure that does not define operational capacity, and the contract says repeating the disputed announcement is not enough.

reviews.rationale: The only evidence is Microsoft's own undefined 'total capacity' figure. There is no commissioning record or independent tally of operational additions for the period, and no evidence of intent either way. The packet cannot settle whether more than 500MW came into service.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps his questioning and his personal-search framing ('I can't find'). It does not turn this into a claim that no other sites exist.

contract.note: The contract correctly treats this as expressed doubt plus a report of his own search, with no objective test that would not inflate the claim.

evidence.note: Reports Guthrie saying several identical Fairwater sites were under construction, without naming locations. This does not test his expressed doubt or what his own search found.

reviews.rationale: The statement questions whether the sites exist and reports that his search found nothing. That doubt is hedged and his private search cannot be checked, so there is nothing to score without making the claim stronger than he did.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: A firm, general industry observation that keeps 'for the most part'. Linking it to the Vineland example matches the context.

contract.note: Reading it as most projects due for full delivery not reaching full scope is ordinary and fair. The Q1 2026 window and count basis are the evaluator's choices, which the flags disclose.

evidence.note: As of Feb 2026, 11GW slated for 2026 showed no visible construction. This is capacity rather than project count and looks forward, so it does not show completion status of projects already due.
57% of projects were delayed 3+ months in 2025. This is a period before the target quarter, and delay is not the same as failing to complete.
Record absorption in North American primary markets in 2025. This is a different period and metric and qualifies the claim without contradicting it.

reviews.rationale: The evidence points to widespread delays and slow construction, but none of it gives a defined project population with due dates and completion status for Q1 2026. The majority claim cannot be confirmed or refuted from this packet.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: This is close to verbatim and keeps the comparison, 'theoretical', and the negative 100% margin. The delay clause frames a vulnerability; it does not make the claim conditional.

contract.note: Treating established cloud applications as existing business is an ordinary reading. The contract admits that the margin basis is unspecified and that a definitive grade depends on settling it.

evidence.note: Software revenue was up 3% in USD and down 1% in constant currency, consistent with a narrow 'plateauing' reading. It says nothing on GPU margins or other business lines.
Company-reported 11% constant-currency growth in cloud applications goes against 'only real growth' from OpenAI deals and GPU compute. It shows growth but not segment profitability.

reviews.rationale: The software line was flat, but applications grew double digits, which cuts against 'only real growth'. The negative 100% GPU margin is unverified, and the profitability needed for the contradiction condition is not shown. The composite claim cannot be graded as a whole on this packet.
